source.name: measured vapour pressures and the critical point
source.fit: 8 measured values (0 from the ThermoML Archive), the normal boiling temperature 518.20 K (Uslu et al., Fluid Phase Equilib. 273 (2008) 21-26, doi:10.1016/j.fluid.2008.08.004 (normal boiling temperature, NIST TRC ThermoML Archive), fitted as 101.325 kPa, never left out) and the critical point, 375.00-766.00 K, max deviation 0.73 %. Between 518.20 K and the critical point the curve is held only by the critical point. The transpiration values of Verevkin et al. (2012, 328-373 K) lie 11-43 % above this curve and are left out: no curve with a physical enthalpy of vaporization meets both them and the measured normal boiling temperature; transpiration takes the vapour as monomer, and a carboxylic acid partly dimerizes in the gas, which makes the apparent pressure too high (a likely reason, not checked). Below 375 K the record refuses. The open liquid densities end at 343 K, so above 375 K the liquid density is refused too (no open data; wanted: densities above 375 K, or vapour pressures between 343 and 375 K by a static or ebulliometric method).
